text:
Mia Chang: quick brain-dump — i'm thinking we should revisit per-node package delegation vs a central relay for air-gapped sites. bandwidth and operator UX are flipping the tradeoffs again.
Samir Patel: +1. per-node pulls reduce central bandwidth but forces each agent to handle complex verification, retry, backoff, and partial resume. more code surface.
Elaine Gomez: concerned about key material & audit. per-node means either we provision signing keys on each host (bad) or we ship signed artifacts and rely on verifier-only agents. we need an attestation chain tied to operator actions.
Mia Chang: agreed. my idea: agents are verifier-only. operator provides a small signed manifest + seed catalog. nodes pull content, verify signatures, and produce a signed apply-record back to the operator (for audit). avoids per-node private keys for signing bundles.
Jonathan Reed: what about sites with strict egress? some customers only allow a single outbound proxy/relay. per-node parallel pulls will overwhelm that.
Samir Patel: that's where a hybrid mode helps: per-node delegation when network allows, otherwise central relay (tiered relay) that streams to local subnet. the relay can apply rate-limits and dedupe downloads.
Mia Chang: sketch of manifest format (minimal):
version: 1
seed: sha256:...
components:
  - name: runtime
    chunk_index: s3://staging/idx/runtime.idx
    signature: sig.v1:...
Samir Patel: + snippet for agent resume semantics: agent keeps a local resume-token per-chunk and reports progress. operator replay can diff resume tokens to avoid re-send.
Elaine Gomez: we must include verifier hooks for KMS/HSM attestation when available. if site provides KMS stub, agent should fetch a public attestation cert and include that in the apply-record.
Jonathan Reed: rollout safety: canary by CIDR + staged activation window. operator should be able to mark a manifest as "activate-if" with a low-risk subset, and have automatic rollback on failed healthchecks.
Mia Chang: open questions:
- how do we throttle per-node pulls in a relay mode? token-bucket per-customer or per-relay?
- what metadata do we include in the apply-record for legal/audit reasons?
- idempotency: what is our canonical apply id?
Samir Patel: proposals: throttle at relay with token-bucket tied to the relay cert. apply-record fields: manifest_id, node_id, resume_tokens[], verified_signatures[], attestation_cert_chain[]. canonical apply id = sha256(manifest_id || node_id || activation-window).
Elaine Gomez: we also need key-rotation semantics: manifest signatures should include signer key id + rotation epoch. operator must publish signer-key history to a signed key-rotation manifest.
Jonathan Reed: failure modes: partial-apply (some components applied, others failed) — operator should support staged activation markers and a deterministic rollback plan. agents should garbage-collect only after operator ack.
Mia Chang: UX note: operator console should show per-node progress and highlight nodes stuck at the same chunk (possible cache miss). add a grpc streaming endpoint for real-time progress.
Samir Patel: implementation plan suggestion:
1) prototype verifier-only agent with resume-token API and signed apply-records.
2) build relay prototype that can dedupe and apply token-bucket throttles.
3) wire in key-rotation manifest and minimal attestation attachment.
4) run chaos tests for partial-apply and relay saturation scenarios.
deploy-bot: artifact-check: package-proto v0.7.1 signed OK (sha256:abcdef... ) :white_check_mark:
Elaine Gomez: +1 to the plan. add a security review gate before the relay goes beta. particularly for the relay's cache integrity and its memory of resume tokens.
Jonathan Reed: i'll draft a short RFC for the per-node resume-token schema + apply-record fields and include test scenarios. will ping infra for a relay perf benchmark.
Mia Chang: sweet. next steps: Jonathan will upload RFC by EOD Tue, Samir will stub the token API, Elaine will list compliance fields we need, i'll sketch the operator console UX. thanks all. :wave:
